findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/emails/rake/console
findings.body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call lives only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so fallback locale files (site default locale and English) are only loaded during controller requests. In every other server-side context that translates — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, user notification emails, rake tasks, console — the translate accelerator's `load_locale` only loads the current locale. When the Fallbacks backend then tries to fall back to e.g. :en for a key missing from the user's locale, the English translations were never loaded into the process, so instead of the English text users get a "translation missing" string (the MissingTranslationData exception is swallowed by I18n's exception handler). Since the stated purpose of the PR is server-side fallbacks, and emails/jobs are the main server-side translation surface, the fallback-chain loading should happen in the accelerator itself (e.g. in `load_locale`/`translate`) rather than in a controller before_filter.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain, leaving stale results when default_locale changes
findings.body: Cached translations are keyed only by `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With the new FallbackLocaleList, a lookup for a key missing in the current locale resolves via `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then :en, and that resolved value is cached under the current locale's key. If an admin later changes `SiteSetting.default_locale`, nothing resets the I18n LRU cache (changing a site setting does not call `I18n.reload!`), so all previously cached fallback results continue to return text from the old default locale until the entries happen to be evicted (300-entry cache) or the process restarts. Consider including the effective fallback list (or default_locale) in the cache key, or clearing the cache when default_locale changes.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback ordering or loading behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces user-visible fallback semantics ([requested locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]) via a custom Hash subclass plus a new per-request loading hook and a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!` API, but contains no spec changes at all. There is nothing pinning down the fallback order, the behavior when a translation exists only in English, or the interaction with the translate accelerator's on-demand loading (the exact area where this can silently break, e.g. in job contexts). At minimum, specs should cover that a missing translation in a non-default locale returns the English string and that the fallback list reflects changes to SiteSetting.default_locale.
